response.consequence: A single-use backup code can authenticate more than once. An attacker who has a leaked code can race the legitimate user and both get in. Consumed codes can also be resurrected by a lost update. The 2FA single-use guarantee is broken. Existing 2FA users have NULL backupCodes and get MissingBackupCodes. That is a separate gap, and the code shown has no backfill or regeneration path for them.
response.explanation: authorize reads user.backupCodes in the initial findUnique. It decrypts the value and checks indexOf in memory. It then sets the entry to null and writes the whole re-encrypted array back with an unconditional update keyed only by user id. There is no transaction, row lock, or compare-and-set on the previous ciphertext. Two concurrent logins that submit the same valid backup code both read the same array, both find the code, and both pass. The later write also overwrites the earlier one, so concurrent use of two different codes can restore a code that was already consumed.
response.title: Backup code consumption is a non-atomic read-modify-write, so one code can be used by concurrent logins
